column1: # test/retrieval-queries.tsv -- the retrieval evaluation query set.
# 59 questions an AGENT would ask in a LATER session about work done in an
# EARLIER one, over the corpus test/retrieval-corpus.sh builds. Derived from
# what that corpus actually says: each one was written by finding a fact
# worth recalling and then phrasing the question the way somebody would ask
# FORMAT: tab-separated, 8 columns, '#' comments and blank lines ignored.
# (Tab-separated and parsed with a delimiter-PRESERVING split, because this
# repo has already been bitten once by strtok_r collapsing empty fields --
# see FINDINGS.md. Empty columns are normal here; `trap` usually is.)
#   id       Q01..Q59, stable. Never renumber: baselines cite these.
#   split    dev | test. `test` is HELD OUT -- 18 of 59 (31%). Do not look
#            at held-out failures while tuning; report them separately.
#   expect   indexed   -- the answer is in something `viki index` covers
#            unindexed -- the answer exists ONLY in an artifact viki does
#                         not index today. These MUST all fail at baseline.
#                         That failure is the coverage-gap measurement, and
#                         when somebody indexes check-in comments these
#                         queries start scoring with no edit to this file.
#   artifact where the answer physically lives: file | wiki | ticket |
#   query    what gets passed to `viki ask`
#   anchor   a literal substring of the GROUND-TRUTH chunk. Ground truth is
#            expressed this way, not as a content_hash#chunk_ix, on purpose:
#            hashes move when a document is edited and chunk_ix moves when
#            chunking changes (an epoch bump), and either would silently
#            invalidate the whole file. The harness resolves anchor ->
#            {content_hash#chunk_ix} against the cache db at run time and
#            prints what it resolved to. An anchor that resolves to NOTHING
#   trap     optional. A literal substring of a STALE or WRONG chunk -- the
#            answer that used to be true. If a trap chunk outranks every
#            gold chunk the harness reports STALE_OUTRANKS, which is the
#            failure mode that matters most for an episodic memory.
# Anchors must sit on ONE line of the source document: chunk_text keeps the
# original hard wrapping, so a phrase that wraps will never match.
